observation_summary: The RegulaFalsiSolver was failing with a TooManyEvaluationsException because it was getting stuck in an infinite loop (or an excessively long one) when the approximation did not improve, rather than detecting the convergence failure.
reasoning_summary: The fix introduces a conditional check (if x == x1) to detect when the algorithm is stuck and throws a ConvergenceException instead of allowing the evaluation count to exceed the limit. This is a classic missing guard/validation check for a boundary condition in an iterative algorithm.
evidence_used: The fix adds an 'if (x == x1)' check inside the RegulaFalsi solver loop.
The test expected a ConvergenceException but received a TooManyEvaluationsException, indicating the solver was not correctly identifying the convergence failure.
The bug report states the solver was getting stuck, requiring a check to detect this state early.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix modifies the loop behavior, the root cause is the absence of a guard condition to detect the 'stuck' state, which is the definition of a Checking defect.
